Glossary

Cohort
A named group of players and one question about them, fixed in advance. Every cohort states what it forecasts, when it freezes, when it settles, and the baseline it must beat.
Freeze
The moment the roster is fixed. After it, nobody is added or removed — so the group cannot be chosen to flatter the result.
Settle
The moment the real outcome is known and the forecast is scored against it.
Baseline
The naive answer the model has to beat, declared before any projection is filed. A forecast that cannot beat its baseline has earned nothing.
Forward claim
A projection filed BEFORE the outcome. The only kind that counts toward the score.
Backtest
A projection about something already decided. Kept and labeled, never counted as a forward hit.
Provisional date
A window the league has not published yet, estimated from the rules or last season. Marked as provisional and corrected when the real calendar lands.

How the ratings are built

Arithmetic, not judgment. The overall rating on a score card is a calculation you could re-run by hand from the same capture the page is built on. A player's is 70% production and 30% availability, each a percentile among players at his position; a club's is the equal-weight mean of record, offence, defense and ball security. Those weights are the whole method. There is no adjustment layer and no number anyone can lean on.

Computed now — not filed, not scored. A rating is not a forecast. Kwotient's forecasts are filed before an outcome and graded against it in public; a rating is arithmetic over what has already happened, and every card says so on its face. The two are never mixed.

Every stat's direction is tested. A rating is only honest if a bad performance lowers it. Ours did not always: interceptions thrown were once ranked like passing yards, so a quarterback's picks raised his rating. That was found and fixed in August 2026, and it moved real players — the correction is in the public repository with the date on it. A standing test now makes each ranked stat worse in turn and requires the rating to fall, so the assumption cannot return unnoticed.

A measure that cannot separate players does not flatter them. Most receivers fumble nothing all season. Ranking them naively would tie almost the whole position for first and hand out a perfect score for doing what everyone did. Percentiles use the midrank instead: keeping the ball like everyone else scores average, and the players who did fumble sit below them.

Why it is written down. Every rating system has been wrong at some point. What a reader is entitled to know is what happens next — whether the error is found, whether it is published with the players it moved, and whether anything is put in place so it cannot recur. This page exists so that can be checked rather than taken on trust.

Terms of use

What this is. Kwotient publishes dated forecasts and scores them against outcomes. Everything here is informational — it is not betting, financial or investment advice, and no figure on this site is a recommendation to wager or trade.

No affiliation. Kwotient is not official league data and is not endorsed by or affiliated with the NBA, NFL, WNBA, any team, any players association, or any data provider named here.

Accuracy. A forecast is a dated opinion, published so it can be judged later — that is the product, not a guarantee. Underlying data is compiled from the sources below on a best-effort basis and may contain errors or revisions; scores are computed against the data as it stood when each forecast was filed, so the record cannot shift after the fact.

Data and attribution. Every source the board reads is named here, and here only — the boards themselves say which capture they show, not where it came from.

  • NFL contract comparables, club identifiers and salary-cap history: Over the Cap, under a direct API license. Comparable-contract figures shown on this site are Kwotient's own analysis of that data.
  • NFL statistics, rosters, depth charts, injuries and the trade log: via nflverse (CC-BY 4.0).
  • NFL advanced boards: Pro-Football-Reference advanced tables and ESPN Total QBR, via nflverse (CC-BY 4.0).
  • NBA statistics, contracts, standings and injuries: BALLDONTLIE, under commercial license.
  • Live scores, previews, in-game updates and recaps: BALLDONTLIE and StoryStats, under paid subscriptions.

Kwotient's own projections, scores and text may be quoted with attribution and a link; the underlying third-party data may not be resold in raw form.
